key_insight: PAIR-IBD spatially quantifies inflammation and crypt injury to distinguish pathologist-defined active ulcerative colitis from histological remission.
clinical_relevance: This ulcerative colitis histology study—not cancer drug discovery—suggests AI could complement pathology scoring and clinical-trial endpoint assessment, pending validation.
method: Train a deep-learning ensemble on three IBD datasets to identify inflammatory cells and segment mucosal compartments.
Quantify compartment-specific cell densities, epithelial damage and crypt architecture.
Compare AI measurements with pathologist-defined disease activity and manual scores.
evidence_signal: Within one clinical network, active biopsies had 5.3-fold higher crypt neutrophil density than Nancy-defined remission; key AI metrics correlated with manual scores (Spearman rs=0.50–0.73).
watch_item: Single-network evaluation limits generalizability; external validation is needed before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Spatial AI quantification of inflammatory and architectural features differentiates pathologist-defined active ulcerative colitis from histological remission
